correctness.rationale: For every complete multipartite graph with r>=3 nonempty parts and balanced signing, a switching gauge epsilon transforms the signed process to the all-positive one. After first ignition x in part P, next simultaneous spread burns every vertex outside P with the same color; at most one additional vertex v within P can be ignited in the opposite color before the last spread, and this is possible precisely when P has size at least two. This proves the full terminal code {+/-epsilon} union {(+/-epsilon)^(v):v in nonsingleton parts}, cardinality 2+2m, and the unsigned weight enumerator 1+z^N+m(z+z^(N-1)). For an arbitrary sign word w the distance to the unsigned code is t-delta(w), t=min(number of positive,number negative) and delta=1 iff an eligible coordinate lies in a smaller sign class; optimizing gives radius floor(N/2) if m=0, N/2-1 if m>0 and N even, and for odd N=2h+1 gives h if s>=h else h-1. The claimed plurality formula then follows from gauge coordinate flips. Independent state-space exploration of all legal spread-first/ignite-after trajectories for 1,044 balanced-signature cases to N=6 corroborated the formula; the universal three-round argument provides the infinite proof.

This is a nontrivial natural classification, not a mere numerical exercise or a renaming of known switching equivariance.
